fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responding units can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entry clearly on both sides so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can identify it quickly.
• Clear a turnaround area near the parking zone large enough for an emergency vehicle to reverse direction without backing the full length of the access drive.
• Trim back dense vegetation along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Cut back shrubs and low-hanging branches where dense vegetation meets the structure to keep a clear path around the building's perimeter.
• Keep the access drive surface free of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so the full width remains usable by responding units.
• If a gate is present at the single entry point, ensure it can be opened quickly from outside without a key or combination.
• Post the property address visibly at the road entrance, not only at the front door, so units do not have to drive to the structure to confirm the address.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Mixed Vegetation; Brush Area; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Limited Rear Access; Scattered Trees
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching any side of the house.
• Remove shrubs and low branches from around the base of the tree cluster closest to the structure.
• Thin the mixed vegetation area nearest the house to create open gaps between plants and the building.
• Clear brush from the brush area closest to any structure or outbuilding on the property.
• Cut back low-hanging branches from scattered trees near the house so they do not hang over the roof or walls.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs along both sides.
• Remove any vegetation growing along the rear of the property that limits movement or visibility close to the structure.
• Maintain the open separation areas that currently exist between vegetation and the structure by keeping them mowed or cleared.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it remains visible to approaching vehicles during low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the rear of the structure accessible by cutting back any shrubs or brush that block movement around the building.
